title: HTTP Caching
body:
Caching is about avoiding the round trip entirely, or at least avoiding re-downloading a body you already have. The check happens on **your machine**, before a request is sent.

`Cache-Control` (set by the server) tells the browser how long a response may be reused — `max-age=3600`, `no-store`, `must-revalidate` and so on. If the entry is still fresh, the browser serves it from cache and no network request happens at all.

`ETag` is a fingerprint of the response body, generated by the server. When a cached copy has gone stale, the browser re-requests with `If-None-Match: <etag>`; if nothing changed, the server replies **304 Not Modified** with no body, which is far cheaper than sending the whole resource again. A [[CDN]] sits in the middle of all of this and applies the same rules at the edge. See [[HTTP Status Code]].
